_about.what: The lede under the h1 on every motorcycle-endorsement state page. One template for the cert, filled from whichever state the page is for.
_about.shape: Each paragraph is a list of sentence slots. A slot is one string, or a list of variants tried in order.
_about.headings: A block may instead be { heading }, which renders an h2 above the paragraphs that follow it. h2 because the page's h1 is the title and a heading level may never be skipped. The value takes placeholders and `when` like any slot, but NEVER a citation marker: a heading labels the paragraphs under it rather than making a claim of its own, and a marker there would number a source ahead of the sentence that earns it. Put the markup in the stylesheet, never in the string - the crude first pass carried an inline font-size.
_about.variants: The first variant whose placeholders ALL resolve is the one used, so a state missing a fact drops to a shorter sentence rather than printing a hole. Order them longest-first. A slot where nothing resolves is skipped, and a paragraph whose slots are all skipped disappears.
_about.placeholders: {group.field} is a fact. A constrained one renders the `long` string from motorcycle-endorsement-display.json; a number renders through format-fact.js. {stateName}, {localTerm}, {agencyCode} and {agencyName} come from the state's meta. A path naming no real fact THROWS at build - it is a typo, not a gap, and the two must not look alike.
_about.when: A variant may carry `when`, requiring a fact to equal an exact value. Several keys may be given and ALL must match. For where a number needs different prose at one value: renewalYears 0 means 'does not expire', never 'every 0 years'.
_about.courseRequired: ONE slot owns the claim that training is required, and no other sentence in this file may restate it - that is what let 'the required training' stand wrong in GA and CA for a fortnight. Three variants: courseRequired true WITH courseRequiredUnderAge for a state where the requirement has an age boundary, courseRequired true without it for a state where it applies to everyone, and courseRequired false for a state where a course is one route of two. The age variant needs no `when` on the number - it carries {criteria.courseRequiredUnderAge} as a placeholder, so it drops itself wherever that fact is null. A state nobody has researched has courseRequired null, matches no gate, and prints nothing.
_about.examRoute: The sentence saying HOW a rider reaches the exam is its own slot, gated on examAdministration plus courseWaivesAgencyExam, and the exam-shape variants under it open with a plain noun phrase. Keeping the route out of the shape stops the two axes multiplying: a new route value costs one variant, not seven.
_about.namingTheExam: Exactly one of the two slots names the exam, and which one depends on whether the state published any exam detail. A `course` state with a null questionCount has nothing for the shape slot to say, so its route variant absorbs the name and the shape slot's bare fallbacks are gated to `agency` and drop - that is why Texas reads as one sentence instead of two thin ones. A `course` state that DID publish detail (Florida) takes the plain route sentence and lets the shape slot name the exam. Both bare fallbacks carry the agency gate; adding a third examAdministration value means revisiting them.
_about.whenNull: A `when` may require a fact to be null, which reads as 'nobody made this claim yet'. Used twice, both to suppress a sentence another slot has already covered. It cannot tell a sourced null from an unsourced one, so only use it to choose a SHORTER sentence - never to assert something a null would have to mean.
_about.sectionedExams: isExamSectioned true gates a parallel set of exam variants, listed FIRST so they win before the plain ones are reached. They deliberately hold passingScorePercent OUT of the exam sentence and state it in the sectioning sentence instead, because a per-section gate printed as a bare score reads as an overall one. Keep the two halves in step when editing either.
_about.ridingSkillsTest: The `course` value deliberately has NO variant, so a state where the course handles the riding evaluation prints nothing rather than a sentence about a test that does not exist. That is the whole point of the value - do not add one to fill the gap. The two agency values are separate sentences because their waivers differ: agencyWaivable is waived by finishing the course, agencyUnlessLicensed is not waivable for a minor at all, and one shared sentence would be wrong for somebody either way. BOTH variants gate on courseWaivesAgencyExam being NULL, meaning the route sentence made no waiver claim of its own. Either non-null value states the skills waiver up there already - true says the course waives knowledge and skills, false says it waives skills only - so a sentence here would repeat one of them. Null still reaches the states that need it: a course-administered exam plus an agency skills test, which is where Texas sits. KNOWN GAP, quiet rather than wrong: a state that waives the skills test BOTH by course and for already-licensed adults prints only the first, and wants a fourth variant rather than an ungated one.
_about.editing: Sentence copy lives here. The phrases that fill a {group.field} slot live in motorcycle-endorsement-display.json under `long`, because one phrase serves every state sharing that token.

paragraphs: In {stateName}, riding legally means holding a {localTerm}, and it's required for {criteria.requirementType}.

paragraphs.text: Certification is handled by the {agencyName} ({agencyCode}). You can apply starting at age {criteria.minAge} with no other license needed beforehand.

paragraphs: Certification is handled by the {agencyName} ({agencyCode}). You can apply starting at age {criteria.minAge} once you already hold a {criteria.minLicense}.

paragraphs.text: {stateName} accepts no out-of-state credential, so you'll test in-state even if you're already endorsed elsewhere.

paragraphs: If you're already endorsed in another state, {stateName} accepts a credential from {criteria.transferOutOfStateEndorsement}.

paragraphs.heading: How do I learn to ride?

paragraphs.text: Riding and road-rules training is required in {stateName} if you're under {criteria.courseRequiredUnderAge}, and taking a course is usually the easier route regardless. Courses are built on the {criteria.courseType} and listed on a {criteria.findCourse}.
The required riding and road-rules training you need in {stateName} is built on the {criteria.courseType}, and courses are listed on a {criteria.findCourse}.
{stateName} doesn't require riding and road-rules training, though taking a course is usually the easier route. Courses are built on the {criteria.courseType} and listed on a {criteria.findCourse}.

paragraphs: Courses will supply you with a bike to learn on. Typically, your course will involve online or classroom informational sessions followed by two days of riding exercises.

paragraphs.text: A course runs around {criteria.classCost}, and the credential itself is {criteria.dmvCost} to {agencyCode}.

paragraphs: Plan to budget around {criteria.classCost} for the course, plus {criteria.dmvCost} to {agencyCode} for the credential.

paragraphs.text: Purchase a full set of gear to wear during every ride, including a DOT-certified full-face or modular helmet. Proper gear will save your life.
Successfully completing the course waives the {agencyCode} knowledge and riding skills exams, so testing directly is the other route.
Successfully completing the course waives the {agencyCode} riding skills exam, but either way you'll need to sit for a knowledge exam.
The course itself is where you're examined, and what you'll take is the {exam.examType}.
The course itself is where you're tested.
The {exam.examType} is {exam.questionCount} questions, with {exam.timeLimitMinutes} permitted for testing.
{stateName}'s {exam.examType} is {exam.questionCount} questions
The exam to prepare for is the {exam.examType}.

paragraphs: The {exam.examType} is {exam.questionCount} questions, requires a score of {exam.passingScorePercent} to pass, and allows {exam.timeLimitMinutes} for testing.
The {exam.examType} is {exam.questionCount} questions, and requires a score of {exam.passingScorePercent} to pass.
The {exam.examType} requires a score of {exam.passingScorePercent} to pass.

split into separately scored sections, {exam.examSectionNames}, and you'll need a {exam.passingScorePercent} on each section to pass.
